content:
- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or shows sharp declines; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to premature reversal in price direction.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing short-term sentiment-driven volatility; sentiment shifts are not fully reflected in 30d forecasts.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating +/–), model tends to average out extremes, underestimating magnitude of swings.
- High sentiment volatility correlates with higher forecast error; model struggles to adapt to rapid sentiment shifts.
- Model often overestimates peak prices in bullish phases, then underestimates subsequent decline — suggesting failure to model sentiment-driven momentum decay.
- When sentiment is strongly positive for 3+ days, model tends to overproject upward trend; should cap forecast growth after 3 consecutive positive sentiment days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative for 3+ days, model tends to underproject downward trend; should adjust downward by 5–10% of recent average if sentiment persists.
